patterns.usage_note: The 参る-based humble/formal counterpart of 〜ていく, pointing forward from the present, which is why it is the standard closing of pledges in speeches, press releases and customer letters. Because 参る is humble, it is used of your own or your organization's actions, or of impersonal developments, not of a respected person's actions. The same forms also serve the 〜てくる sense (progress up to now); direction is read from context and tense.

examples.ruby: 今後[こんご]も品質[ひんしつ]の向上[こうじょう]に努[つと]めてまいります。
examples.english: We will keep working to improve our quality going forward.

examples.ruby: この技術[ぎじゅつ]はこれからさらに身近[みぢか]なものになってまいります。
examples.english: This technology is going to keep becoming more and more a part of everyday life.

examples.ruby: 一杯[いっぱい]ずつ心[こころ]を込[こ]めてコーヒーを淹[い]れてまいります。
examples.english: We will go on brewing every single cup with care.

patterns.usage_note: Continuation or gradual change heading away from the present moment or from where the speaker stands; it is the mirror image of 〜てくる, which tracks change accumulating up to now. 〜てく／〜でく is the casual spoken contraction, and 〜てまいります the formal humble version. With motion verbs it keeps its literal 'do it and go' reading.

examples.ruby: この村[むら]の人口[じんこう]はこれからも減[へ]っていくだろう。
examples.english: This village's population will probably keep shrinking from here on.

examples.ruby: 十月[じゅうがつ]に入[はい]ると、朝[あさ]の風[かぜ]は冷[つめ]たくなっていく。
examples.english: Once October comes around, the morning wind gets colder and colder.

examples.ruby: 傘[かさ]は重[おも]いから、ここに置[お]いてくね。
examples.english: The umbrella's heavy, so I'll just leave it here and head off.
